context.title: Global Electricity Access and Deficit Overview
context.goal: Monitor global and regional progress in electricity access rates across urban and rural populations and evaluate the total population lacking access from 2000 to 2019 to inform energy development initiatives.
context.audience: Global development analysts, international energy policy planners, and executive stakeholders.

datasets.summary: Annual country-level electricity metrics spanning 2000 to 2019 across 6 global regions, tracking overall, urban, and rural electrification percentages alongside absolute population counts without access.

derived_fields.name: urban_rural_access_gap
derived_fields.expression: urban_pct - rural_pct
derived_fields.description: Percentage point gap between urban electrification access and rural electrification access.

kpis.name: Average Access to Electricity
kpis.description: Mean overall electricity access rate across reporting countries and years.

kpis.name: Average Urban Access Rate
kpis.description: Mean electricity access percentage within urban populations.

kpis.name: Average Rural Access Rate
kpis.description: Mean electricity access percentage within rural populations.

kpis.name: Total Population Without Access
kpis.description: Cumulative count of people without electricity access across evaluated countries.

kpis.name: Average Urban-Rural Access Gap
kpis.description: Mean percentage point differential between urban and rural electrification rates.

kpis.name: Reporting Countries
kpis.description: Distinct count of tracked countries in the dataset.

thresholds.name: Critical Low Access
thresholds.description: Highlights country observations where overall electricity access falls below 50%.

thresholds.name: Severe Deficit Scale
thresholds.description: Identifies records where 10 million or more people lack electricity access.

glossary.definition: The percentage of the total national population that has access to electricity.
The percentage of urban residents with access to electricity.
The percentage of rural residents with access to electricity.
The total number of individuals in a country lacking electricity connection.
The arithmetic difference between urban and rural electrification rates, indicating infrastructure disparity.

sections.title: Executive Overview: Global Electrification Status
sections.purpose: Provide senior stakeholders with a high-level summary of worldwide electrification progress, total population deficits, and coverage across countries.

questions.text: What is the global average electricity access rate across tracked countries and years?
questions.rationale: Establishes the primary baseline for worldwide energy access progress.

questions.text: What is the total population currently living without access to electricity across all reporting regions?
questions.rationale: Quantifies the absolute scale of the energy deficit to prioritize international aid.

questions.text: How many reporting countries are actively monitored across the 2000 to 2019 reporting period?
questions.rationale: Provides visibility into dataset coverage and geographic tracking scope.

sections.title: Geographic and Regional Deficit Distribution
sections.purpose: Evaluate spatial disparities in electricity access rates and locate regions bearing the highest burden of unserved populations.

questions.text: How does average electricity access compare geographically across countries and regions on a global map?
questions.rationale: Identifies territorial disparities and highlights clusters with critically low access rates.

questions.text: Which regions and countries account for the largest volumes of people without access to electricity?
questions.rationale: Directs capital investments to areas with the highest concentrated deficits.

questions.text: Which countries consistently report average electrification rates below the critical 50% threshold?
questions.rationale: Flags severe infrastructure deficits requiring urgent multilateral intervention.

sections.title: Urban vs. Rural Disparities and Longitudinal Trends
sections.purpose: Analyze electrification progress over time from 2000 to 2019, contrasting urban infrastructure expansion against rural access gaps.

questions.text: How has overall electricity access evolved year-over-year from 2000 through 2019 across key nations?
questions.rationale: Measures 20-year progress and recovery trajectories across developing economies.

questions.text: What is the average urban-rural access gap across reporting nations, and how pronounced is rural exclusion?
questions.rationale: Evaluates equity between metropolitan centers and rural interior communities.

questions.text: How have rural electrification rates changed over the past two decades relative to urban access?
questions.rationale: Tracks whether rural connection initiatives are closing the gap with urban centers.

context.title: Global Electricity Access Executive Overview
context.goal: Track and analyze long-term trends in global, urban, and rural electricity access rates and the total population living without electricity across regions and countries from 2000 to 2019.
context.audience: Global development analysts, international policy makers, and executive leadership.

datasets.summary: Country- and region-level annual observations from 2000 to 2019 reporting overall electricity access percentage, urban access percentage, rural access percentage, and population count lacking electricity access.

thresholds.description: Identifies records where overall electricity access falls below 50%.

thresholds.name: High Population Without Access
thresholds.description: Flags country-year observations with 10 million or more people lacking electricity.

glossary.definition: The percentage of the total national population that has access to electricity.
The percentage of the urban population that has access to electricity.
The percentage of the rural population that has access to electricity.
The estimated absolute number of individuals living without electricity access.
The disparity measured in percentage points between urban and rural access rates (urban_pct minus rural_pct).

sections.title: Global Access & Population Deficit Overview
sections.purpose: Provide leadership with high-level summary KPIs and macro trends in worldwide electricity access and unserved populations.

questions.text: What is the global average electricity access rate, and how has it progressed over time?
questions.rationale: Establishes baseline performance and overall pace of electrification across reporting years.

questions.text: How many total people currently lack access to electricity globally, and how has this deficit changed?
questions.rationale: Quantifies the absolute population deficit to evaluate international electrification progress.

questions.text: How do access rates compare across major geographic regions in recent years?
questions.rationale: Identifies regional disparities to pinpoint which areas require targeted policy support.

sections.title: Urban vs. Rural Disparities
sections.purpose: Examine the electrification gap between urban centers and rural areas across countries and regions.

questions.text: What is the average disparity between urban and rural electricity access rates over time?
questions.rationale: Tracks whether the development gap between cities and countryside is closing.

questions.text: Which countries have achieved the largest gains in rural electrification?
questions.rationale: Highlights successful country strategies where rural infrastructure expanded significantly.

questions.text: How does urban access stability compare to rural access volatility across key partner nations?
questions.rationale: Surfaces vulnerabilities where rural grids lag behind universal urban adoption.

sections.title: High-Deficit Countries and Critical Need Focus
sections.purpose: Isolate priority countries with acute access deficits to drive targeted capital allocation and policy intervention.

questions.text: Which countries account for the highest concentration of people without electricity?
questions.rationale: Directs leadership attention to high-deficit nations driving the global unserved total.

questions.text: Which countries fall below the critical low access threshold of 50% overall electrification?
questions.rationale: Identifies severely underserved countries requiring urgent international development aid.

questions.text: How have unserved population counts evolved year-over-year in the top deficit nations?
questions.rationale: Evaluates whether electrification efforts in critical countries are keeping pace with population growth.

Component property path keys are semantic contract paths and are preserved; only filesystem paths are removed.
The API oracle supplies empty display samples, recomputes pseudonymized processed-source hashes, rechecks reconciliation, and replays only recorded approved drops through the decision endpoint.
Draft rows are reconstructed from the final persisted Blueprint; status/issue_ids are left as recorded for code to recompute.
